important.name: --committed still measures 'the cut' from the merge base and fast-forwards foreign history
important.summary: The module docstring now defines the cut as the oldest HEAD reflog entry (line 11) and says history the cut commit carried that the target lacks stays behind, then says --committed refuses a target that moved since the cut (line 15). move_committed (105-119) ignores the cut point and uses merge-base(head, target): for a worktree cut from a commit the target never held (the case this PR fixes for staged mode), base == target_head passes, the target fast-forwards onto the cut commit's whole foreign history, and the reported count includes those commits.
fix: In move_committed, compute cut_point(worktree, head) and refuse when it exists and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <cut> <target_head>` fails, pointing to the default staged mode.
Or state in the module docstring that --committed carries the cut commit's history onto the target, and that only the default mode leaves it behind.

important.name: cut_point trusts the oldest surviving reflog entry, which after reflog expiry is not the cut
important.summary:
cut_point takes shas[-1] of the worktree's HEAD reflog as the commit the worktree was cut from, and only checks that it is an ancestor of HEAD. Once gc expires old entries (gc.reflogExpire, 90 days by default; per-worktree HEAD logs are expired too), the oldest surviving entry is a later commit of the worktree's own history. It still passes the ancestry check, so patch_base measures from it, the patch silently omits every commit made before that point, and attach then removes the worktree, leaving those commits dangling on a detached HEAD. The docstring's claim that the oldest entry is the cut holds only while the creation entry survives.

Also (overall): patch_base prefers the oldest HEAD reflog entry whenever it is an ancestor of HEAD. If the worktree merged, rebased onto or switched to a newer target commit B after the cut A, the patch is measured from A and carries the target A..B changes. When the target then reverts part of B (say deletes a file B added), git apply --3way re-creates it: the revert is undone and staged. The old merge-base rule measured from B and was correct. Contradicts the docstring (10-14), a-w SKILL.md:31 and migrating-off-a-plugin SKILL.md:40 (never reverted, conflicts only on paths the worktree changed). Untested.

Also (overall): Reflog entries expire (gc.reflogExpire, 90 days, via gc --auto). On an old worktree the oldest surviving entry can be its own commit W2, which passes the is-ancestor check, so the changes of the earlier commit W1 are left out of the patch, the attach reports success and remove_worktree force-removes the detached worktree, orphaning W1. The merge-base rule could not lose committed work this way.
fix: Accept the oldest entry only when it is the creation entry: read the file at `git rev-parse --git-path logs/HEAD` and require its first line's old oid to be all zeros (new_worktree.py creates it with `worktree add --detach`), else return None and fall back.
Have new_worktree.py record the cut sha at creation (for example a file under the worktree's git dir or `git config --worktree`), and have patch_base read that record before the reflog.

In patch_base also compute the merge base and use the cut point only when it is NOT an ancestor of that merge base (a foreign or squash-merged cut), else the merge base. Add a test: target adds X.txt, worktree fast-forwards to it and adds mine.txt, target deletes X.txt, attach stages only mine.txt.

Trust the reflog only when its first line (git rev-parse --git-path logs/HEAD) has an all-zero old sha, the creation entry, else return None. Add a test that drops that first line after two worktree commits and asserts both files are staged.

minor.name: README option table and hpy order still present the python option as reaching scripts
minor.summary: The new README paragraph (lines 259-262) says the shell skill commands run in does not receive the harness `python` option, so hpy falls through to PATH python. The same section still says otherwise: the harness options table (line 245) describes `python` as 'Interpreter for harness scripts and hooks', and the hpy order (line 252) lists 'HARNESS_PY (project settings env), then the python option' with no qualifier, while line 259 now also allows HARNESS_PY in ~/.claude/settings.json. Hooks do receive CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_* (bash_discipline.py, session_rules.py), so the option works for hooks only. A reader of the table gets the contradicted contract first.

README.md line 252: change '`HARNESS_PY` (project settings `env`), then the `python` option' to '`HARNESS_PY` (settings `env`), then the `python` option (hooks only)'.

minor.summary:

minor.name: a-w docs omit the merge-base fallback of the patch base
minor.summary: a-w SKILL.md line 31 states the staged patch is measured 'from its cut commit, not from the merge base with the target' unconditionally, and migrating-off-a-plugin SKILL.md line 40 promises that a cut from another branch or a squash-merged base 'still attaches'. The code (attach_worktree.py patch_base, lines 171-178; cut_point lines 161-168) uses the oldest HEAD reflog entry only when it exists and is an ancestor of HEAD, and otherwise falls back to the merge base with the target. With an expired or unusable reflog the old merge-base behavior returns, which is exactly the squash-merge case the migrating skill now says is safe. The module docstring (lines 10-12) documents the fallback; the skill prose does not.
fix: In plugins/harness/skills/a-w/SKILL.md line 31, after 'from its cut commit' add '(the oldest entry of its HEAD reflog; without a usable reflog, the merge base with the target)'.
In .claude/skills/migrating-off-a-plugin/SKILL.md line 40, qualify 'still attaches' with 'while the worktree's HEAD reflog still holds the cut commit'.

minor.name: Reflog-fallback test cannot tell the merge base from the target head
minor.summary:
test_staged_without_a_reflog_falls_back_to_the_merge_base deletes logs/HEAD but leaves the target at the cut commit, so the merge base, the target HEAD and the cut point are all repos['base']. A fallback that used the target head (or any of these) instead of the merge base would pass the same assertions; the test only proves that some fallback exists.

Also (tests): cut_point (plugins/harness/skills/a-w/commands/attach_worktree.py:161-168) rejects the oldest reflog entry when it is not an ancestor of HEAD (the worktree was reset or switched elsewhere after the cut) and falls back to the merge base. The new tests cover a usable reflog and a missing reflog, not this third path, so dropping the --is-ancestor guard would go unnoticed.

Also (tests): test_staged_from_a_foreign_cut_with_no_edits_has_nothing_to_move asserts the exit code, the message and that wt survives, but not that the target index stayed empty; the sibling success test checks _staged(main), this one does not.

Also (overall): In test_staged_without_a_reflog_falls_back_to_the_merge_base the cut commit equals the merge base, so the result is the same whichever base is used. It only proves a missing logs/HEAD does not crash.
fix: Move the target before attaching (e.g. _commit(main, 'other.txt', 'other', 'target edit')) and assert _staged(main) == ['a.txt'] and that other.txt is not staged as a deletion; a base taken from the target head would then stage a reverse of other.txt or fail.

Add a test that commits in wt, then runs git -C wt switch --detach to a commit on an unrelated orphan or sibling history (or reset --hard to a commit not descending from the cut), makes an edit, attaches, and asserts only the edit is staged.
Add assert _staged(repos['main']) == [] and assert not (repos['main'] / 'foreign.txt').exists().
Use the foreign-cut helper, delete logs/HEAD, and assert foreign.txt is staged with the worktree file, proving the merge base was used.

minor.name: Settings-path wiring of the new interpreter warning is untested
minor.summary: The new tests call configured_python(path) and check_interpreter(environ, configured) directly, but the only production caller, run_checks (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/doctor.py:197-200), builds the settings path from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude and passes it through. No test reaches run_checks, so a wrong path (wrong file name, ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, dropping the configured argument) would leave the feature silently dead while every test in the PR still passes.
fix: Add a test that writes settings.json under tmp_path / 'cfg' with pluginConfigs['harness@x'].options.python set to a non-existent interpreter, calls doctor.run_checks(make_project(None), {'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR': str(tmp_path / 'cfg')}), and asserts the 'interpreter' check (via _by_name) is WARN with that path in its detail.
